summary: Ran all 13 tests against a bytewise copy of the gate in a /tmp sandbox (junit-platform-launcher directly, one test per launch, with lib.sh's fail/warn/ok instrumented so each test's ACTUAL refusal reason is visible) and put 18 mutations of scripts/check-reviewed.sh and scripts/review_rounds.py through them. Baseline 13/13 green. Every one of the 13 reaches the code path its name claims -- verified from the trace, not inferred: the ten 'does NOT lift the cap' tests all refuse on 'review round N exceeds ... cap of 2', the disagreement test refuses on the disagreement message, and neither the roles check nor 'nothing staged' fires for any of them. Killed: cap block disabled (9 tests die), cap at 1 (1), $TASK dropped from the key (2), worktree read instead of the staged diff (5), key accepted with no reason (1), every diff line matched instead of only added ones (1), `finish` inserted after the argued `warn` (1), BRE filename guard + staged-content read (2), staged-content read alone (3), disagreement resolved instead of refused (1), `|| echo 0` restored (1), `--task` printing nothing (4), index-membership guard + worktree content (4). That is a genuinely strong suite on the escape's core, and the earlier rounds' r1-2 (index vs worktree) and r1-3 (an argued cap still blocks a major) are both now pinned rather than prose. Also independently re-verified the two numbers earlier rounds fought over: `git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed` returns exactly NINE (0837f34, 44400b5, 74254f6, d9a3c22, 6871e7f, 3a5ed79, 461dd53, 2953b5a, 2e0f1d9), and grouping distinct diff_sha256 by task across .harness/review gives 22 over the cap with M4.12 at 12 and M0.13 at 11 -- 22 of 81 today rather than 79, which is exactly the drift the dated sentence anticipates. Two mutations survive that I judge major, both demonstrated end to end rather than argued: nothing pins WHICH FILE the argument must live in, and the new no-task refusal has no test at all.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION: delete ` -- baselines/review.txt` from scripts/check-reviewed.sh:131 (the pathspec on `git diff --cached`). 13/13 green. The suite pins the KEY three separate ways -- exact task not a pattern (aTASKNameIsMatchedEXACTLY), a reason required (aROUNDSKeyWithNOREASON), another task's key rejected (anArgumentForADIFFERENTTask) -- and pins the FILE the argument must live in zero ways. Every fixture that stages an argument stages it in baselines/review.txt, and every fixture that does not stage one stages no `rounds:` text anywhere, so no test can tell 'the added line is in baselines/review.txt' from 'the added line is anywhere in the staged diff'. Measured, not reasoned: in a scratch repo with 3 recorded rounds and NO baselines/ directory at all, I staged `rounds:M9.1  argued in a file that is not baselines/review.txt` as a second line of docs/internal/product/backlog.md. The unmutated gate refuses ('review round 3 exceeds ... cap of 2', exit 1). With the pathspec dropped it prints `WARN review round 3 exceeds the cap of 2, ARGUED as 'rounds:M9.1' in baselines/review.txt` and `ok ... (round 3 of 2)`, exit 0 -- a gate naming a file it never read. review.md rule 12, as amended by THIS commit, states the criterion as 'keyed rounds:<task> in a staged baselines/review.txt'; the file half of that sentence is unconstrained, and it is the half that makes the escape greppable in the one file review.md rule 9 and the baseline's own header point an author at.
findings.failure_scenario: A later tidy-up of that awk pipeline drops or mistypes the pathspec (or someone generalises it to `git diff --cached | awk ...` while adding a second baseline file). Every test stays green. From then on any staged file containing `rounds:<task>  <anything>` waives the round cap -- a line in backlog.md, a comment in the very source file under review, a fixture string in a test -- and the gate reports it as ARGUED in baselines/review.txt, so the trace the whole design exists to leave in the tree points at a file that does not contain the argument. The one added test is the mirror of anArgumentForADIFFERENTTask: stage a well-formed `rounds:<task>  <reason>` line in a file that is not baselines/review.txt and assert the gate still refuses. ⚠️ M4.31's row already records that adding a method here re-keys all thirteen red records, so arguing this as `test-reviewer:T1` in baselines/review.txt with a backlog row (review.md rule 9) is a legitimate resolution and may be the proportionate one at this round -- but landing it silently unpinned is not, because the row's own coverage list reads as though the baseline file were the pinned part.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION: replace the new no-task refusal guard `if [ -z "$TASK" ] && ls ".harness/review/$SHA."*.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then` with `if false; then` -- i.e. delete the whole four-line block this commit adds. 13/13 green. No fixture in the file ever writes a verdict whose `task` is empty, so nothing exercises the branch. Measured end to end: a scratch repo with FIVE recorded rounds whose verdicts all carry `"task": ""` -- exactly what `review.sh record` writes when `--task` is omitted, which M4.29's row records as reachable by typo as easily as by intent. The unmutated gate refuses with 'verdicts exist for the staged bytes but name no task -- recorded without --task'. With the block deleted it prints `ok staged bytes reviewed by reviewer test-reviewer (round 0 of 2)`, exit 0 -- round 0 over five recorded rounds, a count the counter's own definition makes impossible, and a complete bypass of the cap this entire commit is about. The tree already claims this behaviour as delivered: M4.29's row says 'M4.21 closed the half visible from the gate (verdicts present with no task now REFUSE)'. It is claimed, shipped, and constrained by nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone simplifying the gate reads those four lines as defensive noise -- TASK is only used by the argue block below, which already guards on `[ -n "$TASK" ]` -- and removes them. The suite stays green and check-mutants (when M0.14 lands) scores this file as covered. The cap then silently stops applying to every task whose verdicts were recorded without `--task`, which today is roughly a quarter of the 393 verdict files in .harness/review (90 carry no task at all, measured). The fixture cost is one line: `scratch` already writes the verdicts, so a variant writing `verdict("", sha)` plus an assertion on 'name no task' is the whole test.

findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION: change `if (f[1] == k && rest ~ /[^[:space:]]/)` at scripts/check-reviewed.sh:143 to `if (index(line, k) > 0 && rest ~ /[^[:space:]]/)` -- a substring match anywhere on the line instead of an exact first-field match. 13/13 green. aTASKNameIsMatchedEXACTLYAndNotAsAPattern kills the REGEX form of this loosening (it uses `rounds:M9x1`, which a BRE `rounds:M9.1` matches) but not the SUBSTRING form, because `rounds:M9x1` does not contain `rounds:M9.1` literally. Nothing pins that the key must be the line's FIRST field.
findings.failure_scenario: A `baselines/review.txt` entry that merely mentions the key inside another entry's prose -- `reviewer:R4  argued; see the rounds:M4.21 discussion above` -- waives the cap under the substring form, and the entry that does it is a finding argument for an unrelated finding. The fixture is one more string in the existing `scratch(dir, 3, ...)` call shape.

findings.summary: The class javadoc and the anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKSAnUnresolvedMajor javadoc both state the design property as 'both-roles-present AND no-unresolved-majors STAY ENFORCED'. Only the majors half is pinned, and it is pinned in a way that cannot distinguish 'checks every required role' from 'checks the first one'. SURVIVING MUTATION: change `for ROLE in $REQUIRED_ROLES; do` at scripts/check-reviewed.sh:170 to iterate only the first role. 13/13 green, because the test writes the identical major to BOTH role files. The both-roles-PRESENT half has no test at all: no fixture in the file ever omits a verdict. It happens to hold structurally today only because the roles loop at lines 27-34 runs BEFORE the cap block, so I could not construct a single-edit mutation for it -- which is why this is minor and not a repeat of r1-3.
findings.failure_scenario: The unresolved-majors loop is narrowed (or the two loops are reordered so the roles check follows the cap block and a `finish` lands after the argued `warn`) and an argued third round then lands carrying a test-reviewer major, or missing the test-reviewer verdict entirely -- which is precisely the state the file's own javadoc says an argued exception is stricter than SKIP for avoiding. Writing the major to the test-reviewer ONLY, rather than to both, closes the first half for free.

findings.summary: Three branches this commit adds to the gate are individually removable with the suite green. (a) delete the whole `case "$ROUNDS" in ''|*[!0-9]*)` digits guard at lines 72-77: 13/13 green. Its sibling protection IS pinned -- changing `2>"$ERRS"` to `2>&1` is killed by verdictsDISAGREEING, because the fallback message replaces the 'disagree' text the test asserts on -- and I confirmed the combination is the documented fail-open: with both edits the gate prints `[: integer expected`, skips the cap block and exits 0 at round 3. So the guard is defence in depth against a regression the suite does catch, which is why this is minor. (b) delete `[ -n "$WHY" ] || WHY="review_rounds.py exited $RC and printed nothing"` at line 66: 13/13 green -- the only fixture that reaches the error path produces stderr, so the empty-stderr fallback is never taken. (c) delete every `echo "         ..."` remedy line from the refusal at lines 151-164: 13/13 green. overTheCapWithNoArgumentTheGateREFUSES asserts only `contains("exceeds")`.
findings.failure_scenario: (c) is the one that matters, because a remedy the code does not implement is this task's entire premise. M4.31's row credits M4.21 with shipping 'the TEXT half' -- the sentence '⚠️ The line must be ADDED by this commit -- an argument sitting in the already-committed file does not carry a later round.' That sentence is the only place an author at the cap learns why `git add baselines/review.txt` on an unchanged file will not help, and no test holds it. A future reword back to the old, false phrasing ('argue the finding with a staged baselines/review.txt entry') is invisible to the suite, and the defect this commit exists to fix returns as prose while the code stays right. One `assertThat(g.output()).contains("ADDED by this commit")` on the existing refusal test costs nothing and re-keys nothing new beyond what T1/T2 already would.

findings.summary: The comment at aROUNDSLineALREADYCOMMITTEDDoesNOTWaiveALATERCap opens '⚠️ THIS PINS THE CONTEXT RENDERING ONLY'. Measured: it does not. The all-diff-lines mutation (match every diff line, not only `^\+`) is killed by the SIBLING test aROUNDSLineAppearingOnlyAsDIFFCONTEXT and NOT by this one -- in this fixture baselines/review.txt is unchanged between HEAD and the index, so it appears in `git diff --cached -- baselines/review.txt` not at all, as context or otherwise. Across my 18 mutations this test dies on a strict subset of what the CONTEXT test dies on (cap disabled, worktree read, staged-content read; the CONTEXT test dies on those plus all-diff-lines and the BRE filename form), so it is currently mutation-redundant with its sibling. The rest of the comment is accurate and honest, and I checked it specifically: it discloses BOTH known-surviving mutations (a MOVED committed line rendering as delete+add re-arms the escape; a landed argument can never carry a later round) and names M4.31 as owning them, and I confirmed the behaviour this test asserts as correct survives M4.31's proposed primitive (present in `git show :` and absent from `git show HEAD:` still refuses here), so the test does not pin a behaviour M4.31 will invert. Every other measured claim in the file's comments checked out: the ROLE-DERIVATION comment is right (review-roles.sh is not copied, the both-roles fallback is what runs, and the ok line confirms it), 'matching the staged file's CONTENT instead left every other test here green' is right (that mutation kills exactly 3 of 13), 'inserting a finish after the warn left all five green' is right (it kills only anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKS), and the decoy-filename measurement reproduces exactly as described.
findings.failure_scenario: A future reader trims what looks like duplicate coverage. Believing this test is the one holding the added-line rendering, they delete aROUNDSLineAppearingOnlyAsDIFFCONTEXT and keep this one -- and the all-diff-lines mutation, the one bypass that made 'the file was touched' equal 'the line was added', stops being caught by anything. A comment describing its own test's coverage wrongly is the defect class this repository keeps finding, here inside the test file written to close an instance of it. Fixing it is one sentence; per review.md rule 11 that is permitted and probably not worth a round on its own.

notes: METHOD, so the measurements are reproducible: /tmp/rev-test-tr-m421 holds a copy of scripts/{check-reviewed.sh,review_rounds.py,lib.sh}, a copy of the staged ReviewRoundCapTest.java, and a Runner that launches each @Test separately via junit-platform-launcher. lib.sh's fail/warn/ok append to a trace file so each test's actual gate decision is visible rather than inferred. The working tree was never edited, staged or unstaged; `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --cached | sha256sum` were re-checked before recording and the hash is unchanged at 71021ff3c1f1.

EVERY TEST REACHES ITS NAMED PATH -- checked because this repository has repeatedly found tests that refuse for an unrelated reason and pass anyway. Traced decisions: withinTheCap -> ok round 2 of 2; overTheCapWithNoArgument, anArgumentForADIFFERENTTask, anUNSTAGED, worktree-only, noReason, taskExactly -> FAIL 'review round 3 exceeds ... cap of 2'; alreadyCommitted, decoy FILENAME, diff CONTEXT -> the same FAIL at round 4 (committing moves the staged bytes, which is why those three re-record verdicts for the new hash -- and I confirmed that without that re-recording they would refuse on a missing verdict instead, the wrong-reason failure their own comments say bit an earlier draft); overTheCapWithASTAGEDArgument -> WARN ARGUED then ok; anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKS -> WARN ARGUED then two FAILs naming blocking/major for both roles; verdictsDISAGREEING -> FAIL naming the disagreement. No test passes because of 'nothing staged' or a missing role.

ASSERTION STRENGTH, checked and NOT filed as a finding because I could not name a production mutation it lets through: eight of the eleven refusal tests assert only `isNotZero()`, with only overTheCapWithNoArgument ('exceeds'), anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKS ('blocking/major') and verdictsDISAGREEING ('disagree') pinning which refusal fired. Every mutation I tried that made those eight refuse for the wrong reason (corrupting $TASK, disabling the argue block entirely, `--task` printing nothing) was killed at suite level by the two tests that assert a PASS, which is what stops the negatives passing vacuously. Worth knowing that the suite's whole falsifiability for the negative cases rests on withinTheCapTheGatePasses and overTheCapWithASTAGEDArgumentTheGatePasses; there is no redundancy behind those two.

TIER: the subject is a bash gate, so a forked process is unavoidable and there is no T0 form of it. `Path.of("..")` for the repo root and `@TempDir` for the scratch match the nine sibling harness suites (HashableTest, ReviewRolesTest, ReviewDeltaTest, CoverageGateTest, FreshCheckoutTest, RedRecordWiringTest, TddPlanScopeTest, ModuleGateTest, ModuleDriftTest). @TempDir resolves to the system temp directory rather than build/tmp, which is testing.md rule 17 -- deliberately NOT filed as a finding, because it is a suite-wide convention this change follows rather than introduces, and fixing it here would be nine files of churn on a task at the round cap. If it is worth closing it is a row of its own. No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no mock, and a broken repo-root resolution would throw NoSuchFileException rather than pass quietly.

TDD RECORDS: check-tdd is listed PASSED in the packet, which means all thirteen binding keys (declaration + comment-stripped non-test remainder, per tdd_scan.key_parts) match red records for the currently staged bytes. On the specific risk the task raises -- two comments rewritten in this diff, and the key drops comments so no re-key is demanded: both rewrites are comment-only and neither changes behaviour, so no substance drifted from what was observed. I verified the rewritten fixture comment is now TRUE rather than merely plausible (the previous version claimed a docs-only diff summons one role; the scratch does not copy review-roles.sh, so the both-roles fallback runs, and the traced `ok` line names both roles). The one comment I do not believe is at line 271 and is filed as T6.

NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: the only test file in the diff is new, and the four modified files are scripts, a standard and the backlog. Nothing in this commit loosens an existing assertion alongside a production change.

OPEN FINDINGS FROM EARLIER ROUNDS, verified as asked: r1-2 (index vs worktree unpinned) is CLOSED -- aROUNDSLineOnlyInTheWORKTREEOfASTAGEDFile kills the worktree read, and it is not redundant with the unstaged test: it uniquely kills an index-membership-guard-plus-worktree-content variant that the unstaged test passes. r1-3 (the design's justifying property prose-only) is CLOSED for the majors half -- anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKS kills `finish` after the argued `warn` -- and open for the both-roles half, filed as T4. r1-1 and r2-1 (the load-bearing number) are CLOSED and independently re-measured here: nine, with the nine commit hashes listed in the summary.

DELIBERATELY NOT RE-FILED, per the task's own instruction and M4.31's row: the MOVED-line rendering (inserting an entry above an already-argued line re-arms the escape) and the landed-argument case (an argued line, once committed, can never carry a later round). Both are real and both are M4.31's. I did confirm the second one is not merely disclosed but consistent with M4.31's proposed replacement primitive, so the test that pins it will not have to be inverted when M4.31 lands.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS A PASS: T1 and T2 are the only two findings I judge to block, and both are the same shape -- a behaviour the tree claims and the suite does not constrain, each demonstrated with a working exploit rather than argued. Either two added test methods, or an argued `test-reviewer:T1`/`test-reviewer:T2` entry in baselines/review.txt with a backlog row, resolves them; M4.31's row already establishes that adding a method to this file re-keys all thirteen red records, so the argue-plus-row route is legitimate and probably the proportionate one at this round. The four minors should be recorded, not fixed (review.md rule 11).
